answer_to_user:
Nestlé (NESN.SW) currently trades at a P/E of ~27.4x (P/B ~7.0x, EV/EBITDA ~16.2x, dividend yield ~3.9%), reported in CHF.

Honest limitation: I can give you the CURRENT multiple, but I could NOT pull a clean multi-year history of Nestlé’s OWN P/E to say whether 27x is above or below its typical range/median — the data source only stores the latest valuation multiple (P/E is derived from the live price), and asking for a 5-year P/E series returned just the latest value, not a per-year track. So I won’t fabricate a decade of history. For a proper "cheap vs its own history" read you would compare today’s 27x against Nestlé’s own multi-year average (historically Nestlé has often traded in a roughly ~20-25x range as a defensive staple), but I can’t confirm that band from this tool. Directionally, a ~27x P/E and ~7x book for a low-single-digit grower looks toward the FULL end rather than cheap, but treat that as a caveated read, not a data-backed own-history percentile.
